findings.evidence: The record's status is 'claimed' and expected_failure says 'Claimed: no cap- skill exists in wave 1 and the tool is not written, so neither run has been performed here.' But the same record carries a measured_run block (by tools/measure.py, commit 710e7b4, clean_exit 1) showing the tool WAS run and failed. Re-running it now (python3 tools/check_adapter_pairs.py --skills .claude/skills) confirms: tools/check_adapter_pairs.py exists, 44 cap-/seam- skills exist today, and the command exits 1 with `pairs_checked=44, single_adapter=0, empty_axis=44, same_model_pairs=44` -- every current cap-/seam- skill fails this criterion right now, with no deliberate breakage needed. The record's own text is false about the current repository, and its status label ('claimed', implying untested) contradicts the measured_run block sitting right next to it in the same record -- the ceremony's own step 3 (measure) requires re-measuring a skill whose criterion can run here, which this one now can.
findings.fix: Re-run tools/measure.py against build-adapter-pair now that cap- skills exist, set status to measured with the real clean/breakage output (today: clean run already fails 44/44 empty_axis), and either fix the 44 cap-/seam- skills' missing differs_in_execution_model fields or record the gap explicitly instead of leaving the stale 'no cap- skill exists' text standing next to a measured_run that contradicts it.

summary: Reviewed 6 build-layer skills row by row against their skill.json data, kb.py show for every distinct cited id, validate_skills.py --only per skill, and live re-execution of every definition_of_done whose status is measured or whose tool exists (build-ceremony, build-definition-of-done, build-entry-conformance, build-evidence-record all reproduced their recorded clean and breakage output exactly; files restored, tree left clean). build-interface-versioning's DoD correctly discloses its missing tool as a claimed gap, so no missing-tool violation. One high-severity fabricated claim found in build-evidence-record (a 'retry three times' rule dressed in an unrelated real quote from F-b1-02). One high-severity stale definition_of_done in build-adapter-pair: its own attached measured_run shows the criterion already fails against the 44 cap-/seam- skills that exist today, but the record still claims untested. 13 low-severity restatement warnings (all confirmed via validate_skills.py) where a skill repeats an agentic-stack (or, once, build-skill-authoring) fact under the identical quote without naming the owning skill. No misquotes beyond the one fabrication, no bare uncited claims, no cannot-fail DoDs beyond the adapter-pair staleness above, and no description trigger clauses found that fail to fire on their skill's actual scope.
